name: Autosomal Recessive Cerebellar Ataxia-Epilepsy-Intellectual Disability Syndrome due to WWOX Deficiency
aliases: WWOX-related Cerebellar Ataxia with Epilepsy and Intellectual Disability

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for WWOX Deficiency Syndrome

criteria.description: Early onset cerebellar ataxia with developmental delay and intellectual disability
Refractory epilepsy with multiple seizure types including tonic-clonic and myoclonic seizures
Biallelic pathogenic variants in the WWOX gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
MRI showing cerebellar atrophy and delayed myelination
EEG abnormalities consistent with epileptic encephalopathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of early onset cerebellar ataxia with intellectual disability and epilepsy plus confirmation of biallelic pathogenic WWOX variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on genetic confirmation due to phenotypic overlap with other neurodevelopmental disorders.

laboratory: Possible mild metabolic abnormalities secondary to seizures
other: EEG demonstrating epileptic encephalopathy with multifocal spikes

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of spasticity predominates over ataxia
Later onset compared to WWOX deficiency

redFlags: Early onset refractory epilepsy with multiple seizure types
Severe global developmental delay with intellectual disability
references: Abdel-Salam GMH et al. WWOX-related neurodevelopmental disorders: expanding the phenotypic spectrum. Eur J Hum Genet. 2020.
Mallaret M et al. WWOX deficiency causes early infantile epileptic encephalopathy. Brain. 2014.
Orphanet: Autosomal recessive cerebellar ataxia-epilepsy-intellectual disability syndrome due to WWOX deficiency. ORPHA:284282.
